# A grouped block naming the same split twice — a copy-pasted line.
#
# Nothing deduplicated it. The guids come back verbatim, `payment_slots` emits
# one slot per entry and the grouped branch claims one split per entry, so the
# same 40.00 split was counted as two settlements of 40.00 each:
#
#   - `amount:` is checked against the sum of the names, so the file is
#     *required* to state 80.00 for money that moved 40.00;
#   - 80.00 against 100.00 owed passes the owed check;
#   - the split is attached to the lot twice, which is idempotent, so the book
#     ends with one settlement of 40.00 while the file asserts 80.00;
#   - and thereafter the block scores two slots against the one split the lot
#     holds, so the invoice is judged changed on every import of an unedited
#     file — unposted, its posting destroyed, rebuilt, for ever.
#
# That last is exactly what slots exist to prevent, so a repeated name is
# refused, as two `Transaction` blocks under one payment already were.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the repeated guid, with nothing
# attached.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 80
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    Transaction "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
      PaymentSplit "8192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445566778"
      PaymentSplit "8192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445566778"
